personality_one_liner: An AI-powered network security guard providing real-time threat detection, OBSERVE-DETECT-EXPLAIN-RESPOND workflows, and instant operational command.

spacing.rule: Generous tactical spacing with vertical rhythm, 16px screen padding, 12px card gaps

do's: Use tactical solid dark surfaces for instant readability
dont's: No heavy blurs that obscure telemetry data

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.purpose: Network security command center showing active status, threat count, live traffic chart, and recent security alerts.

states.loading: Centered loading spinner with tactical pulse
states.error: Failed to sync telemetry with daemon. Retry.

screens.layout: Sticky header with shield indicator, metrics summary cards in 2x2 grid, live traffic volume sparkline graph, and scrollable list of recent threat alerts with quick AI explanation triggers.

screens.name: Devices
screens.purpose: List all connected Wi-Fi and ethernet devices with IP, MAC, status, and risk level grading.

states.empty: No devices discovered on current subnet scan

screens.layout: Search & filter pill row at top, vertical card list with device avatar badge, risk badge (Low/Medium/High), IP/MAC metadata, and quick action toggle.

screens.name: Network Traffic
screens.purpose: Monitor active connections, top communicating IPs, protocol ports, and real-time bandwidth volume.
screens.layout: Tabbed filter for Connections / Ports / IP Stats, interactive metric gauges, and detailed real-time log rows.

screens.name: Threat Alerts
screens.purpose: Chronological stream of security anomalies with severity grading, detection reasons, and evidence.

states.empty: Zero security anomalies detected. Network secure.

screens.layout: Severity filter chips (All, High, Medium, Low), card items with severity color-coding, timestamp, evidence summary, and 'Analyze with AI' button.

screens.name: AI Threat Explanation
screens.purpose: Human-readable threat analysis breaking down what happened, why it's suspicious, evidence, and recommended actions.

states.empty: Select an alert to generate AI analysis

screens.layout: Structured card stack displaying Event Summary, Suspicion Breakdown, Evidence Table, Potential Threat Classification, and Sticky Action Footer (Block Device / Isolate / Dismiss).

screens.name: DNS Security
screens.purpose: Monitor DNS queries, block suspicious domain resolutions, and track devices querying blacklisted FQDNs.

states.empty: No DNS queries intercepted in current window

screens.layout: Top summary banner of blocked domains, filterable list of query logs with domain, requesting device, and action taken (Allowed / Blocked).

screens.name: Firewall
screens.purpose: Manage blocked devices, configure allow/block rules, and trigger secure isolate actions with safety confirmation.

states.empty: No firewall rules or blocked devices active

screens.layout: Segmented control for Blocked Devices vs Active Rules, action buttons for manual IP block, and modal confirmation dialogs for destructive actions.

screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: Configure monitoring parameters, alert sensitivity thresholds, API endpoints, and network interfaces.
screens.layout: Grouped preference sections with switches, dropdown selectors for scan frequency, backend API URL input, and database export/reset actions.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build NetSentinel AI as an Expo React Native mobile app in /app/frontend using Dark-First Utility styling. Ensure all 8 screens are fully functional with realistic mock data, persistent local storage, interactive threat analysis via simulated AI service layer, and firewall block/isolate confirmation workflows. Adhere strictly to the dark obsidian theme, high-contrast utility colors, 44pt touch targets, and full safe-area compliance.
